topic: market signal review and strategy implications
hypothesis: The skills.sh install counter is a per-repo event counter replicated onto each listing of that repo (repo-level fan-out), not a per-listing count. Therefore (a) the '+160% / x2.60' board inflation factor measured in cycles 69-70 is an artifact of summing a repo-level counter N times, and (b) the correct market-size estimator must be computed at repo-event granularity, not listing granularity - yielding a materially smaller, and rank-different, market.

display_rounding_manufactures_ties.note: 75.6% of page values within +/-50 of exact lifetime; block model in cycles 69-70 ran on the rounded side
display_rounding_manufactures_ties.implication: cycles 69-70 tie counts are inflated ~8x by display rounding

h70_increment_validation_decomposed.implication: cycle 70's 1.10x over-merge correction is unsupported and must not be carried forward

co_movement_is_repo_scoped.implication: counter is broadcast within a repo; mirrored storefronts are independent demand pools, not double-counted installs

dispersion_grows_with_catalog_size.implication: fan-out replication, not per-listing demand, produces the board shape

merge_rule_arbitrariness.implication: x2.602 is one arbitrary point in a range wider than the entire published band 69.1M-125.5M

ranking_is_catalog_size_artifact.implication: install-sum rankings measure catalog breadth, not demand

estimator_disagreement_on_identical_data.implication: estimators disagree 45%+; market size is currently a choice, not a measurement

implications: Withdraw the 69.1M-125.5M install band and the x2.60 factor: both supports fail (rounded input, and a validation that accepts proportional similarity rather than shared install events).

Skills.sh install sums and top-20 rankings are catalog-size and replication signals, not demand signals; do not use them for market sizing or category-growth inference without de-replication and density normalization.

Move competitor ranking to density (installs per distinct counter) as primary, raw sum as labeled catalog-size context; forcedotcom/sf-skills moves #42 -> #247 and sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills holds 11.4% of listings for 0.3% of mass.

Mirror storefronts (55.5% of raw mass) are independent demand pools (cross-repo same-name increment corr 0.042), so cross-repo de-duplication would wrongly discard real installs - the opposite of the cycle 69/70 assumption.
Market size should be published as an estimator range with the rule named, never as a point figure; exact-tie collapse (x=1.189) is the conservative floor until the estimator question is settled.
risks: Over-collapse risk: if a repo genuinely has many independently-installed skills, co-movement clustering understates the market - guard by reporting all three estimators side by side.

Completeness risk: the exact-lifetime corpus covers 5847 listings / 2181 repos while the board census is 19831 listings / 430 repos, so estimator behaviour on the dense 200+ listing repos is inferred rather than measured.

Parser risk: the repo-page parser converts 'K/M' display strings to numerics; 4 of 4 back-to-back probe repos showed page value != exact lifetime (microsoft/azure-skills microsoft-foundry: page 576,600 vs exact 576,429), so any new crawl must capture raw strings plus exact listing-page lifetimes.
Scope risk: skills.sh may change its counter semantics without notice, invalidating cross-cycle comparisons; all cycles to date assume a stable counter definition.
Publication risk: the 69.1M-125.5M band must not be resurrected downstream by a stale artifact - it should be explicitly marked withdrawn in the intel stream.

next_experiment.name: repo-event granularity re-baseline on the 130 head repos
next_experiment.design: Re-crawl the 130 head repos at listing-page granularity to build an exact-lifetime board, then compute three estimators side by side (exact-tie collapse, co-movement clustering at increment correlation >= 0.8, 5% value-proximity) with per-repo decomposition, and re-rank the top 50 by raw vs density.
next_experiment.falsification: If the co-movement estimator lands within 10% of value-proximity on the full head board, the fan-out hypothesis is wrong and the cycle 70 band is reinstated with its original correction.
next_experiment.kill_criterion: Drop the fan-out hypothesis if within-repo increment correlation is not materially above cross-repo same-name correlation; currently 0.748 vs 0.042, an 18x gap.
next_experiment.instrument_fix: E72: capture raw display strings (not parsed numerics) and exact listing-page lifetimes; verify against 4 back-to-back probe repos where page and exact values differ.

diff_from_prev_cycle: Reverses cycle 70's central claim: the x2.60 factor and the 69.1M-125.5M band are withdrawn rather than narrowed, because both of cycle 70's supports fail.
Identifies the mechanism cycle 70 could not see: repo-level counter fan-out (within-repo increment corr 0.748 vs cross-repo same-name 0.042), rather than duplicate-install-event merging.
Establishes that the cycles 69-70 block model ran on display-rounded values, inflating apparent ties ~8x (25.8% vs 3.1% exact-tie rate).
Reproduces cycle 70's 51.8% headline exactly (1,213/2,340) and then decomposes it: 0 pairs share an install event, 100% are only proportionally similar.

Quantifies estimator arbitrariness (x 1.189-2.946 at 5%) as larger than the entire published uncertainty band, making granularity choice a first-class analytical object rather than an implementation detail.
Supplies the competitive-ranking consequence cycle 70 did not reach: density re-ranking, top-20 overlap 15/20, forcedotcom/sf-skills #42 -> #247, and the sickn33 listing-share anomaly.
kill_criterion: Drop the repo-level fan-out hypothesis if, on the exact-lifetime head board, within-repo increment correlation is not materially above cross-repo same-name correlation.
artifact_built_this_cycle: Read-only re-analysis of cached crawl artifacts (430-repo census, 4,516+ exact-lifetime listing records, cycle 70 delta-structure and block-model outputs), plus 4 live read-only probe fetches against skills.sh repo/skill pages for ground-truth validation. No external writes; no new crawling beyond validation probes.
confidence: high on mechanism (18x correlation gap, 4/4 probe agreement), medium on magnitude (three estimators disagree 45%+ on identical data), deliberately not quantified beyond that
